ruling.recommended_action: Route to Ryde human safety review: obtain the rider's detailed account (timing and content of the comments, log of any contact request) and the driver's full statement; make no fare adjustment on the route (17.1 km actual vs 17.2 km optimal, fixed fare) pending the safety review, and record the outcome against the driver's account history.
ruling.reasoning: The dispute is filed as a safety incident: the rider alleges the driver made repeated comments about her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe [F1][F2]. The record contains no in-app chat at all [F3], so the alleged remarks are not captured anywhere; the only rebuttal on record is the driver's post-trip written statement, "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]. That statement is a party's account of an unwitnessed verbal exchange and cannot settle whether unwanted sexual remarks were made; the trace correctly bars automatic ruling on this element and leaves escalate as the permitted outcome (SAFE-1).
ruling.escalation_reason: A rider-filed safety complaint alleging unwanted sexual remarks and a request for her contact details [F1][F2] has no corroborating record — the trip's chat log is empty [F3] and the sole contrary account is the driver's own post-trip statement [F4]. Whether the remarks were made cannot be determined on this record, and SAFE-1/Safe-2 require a human safety reviewer; the human should verify the timing and content of the alleged remarks, any contact request, and obtain a full driver statement. The route itself shows no deviation (17.1 km actual vs 17.2 km optimal) and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote, so no fare adjustment arises [F1][F2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate requested no_action, but the safety allegation of unwanted sexual remarks and a request for her number [F1][F2] is neither recorded nor refuted: there is no chat record [F3] and only the driver's own post-trip denial [F4], so no_action cannot be granted; the case must go to a human under SAFE-1.

The driver advocate requested no_action on the strength of the driver's statement that nothing inappropriate happened [F4], plus an untroubled route (17.1 km vs 17.2 km optimal) and clean profiles [F5][F6]. Profiles and the driver's own denial cannot dispose of a harassment allegation that the record does not capture [F3]; SAFE-1 requires escalation rather than a finding for the driver.

ruling.evidence_gap: The safety elements rest on an unwitnessed verbal exchange: the fact table records no in-app chat messages between rider and driver [F3], and the only other account is the driver's post-trip written denial [F4]. There is no contemporaneous record of what was said, when in the 22:29–22:54 trip it was said, or whether any request for the rider's number was made, so the harassment allegation cannot be verified from the file.
